body.justification: This question isolates the exact effective geometric package still needed to turn coherent recession operators into a finite globally honest search space.
body.gap: Common-ray path independence and single-chart estimates do not establish canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, compatibility on simultaneous collars, translated-uniform tails, or a computable refinement schedule with a vanishing total ledger.
body.consumer: Only an affirmative answer, or a separately proved sufficient gluing package, can supply the displayed premise of the conditional CertGluePFL termination theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation of every active \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and protected star; safety of every positive-weight candidate; simultaneous-collar compatibility; translated-uniform tails; and an input-computable refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes and for which \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
obligation.obstruction: The available finite active-set geometry controls forward motion from a fixed mean, but it does not show that canonical sections preserve every active semantic region and the separated-risk set throughout protected stars. Equality of shared face vertices does not control the actual face--cone rules on simultaneous collar supports. The frozen assumptions also provide neither translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bounds nor a recurrence for the growing number of charged refined cells.
obligation.attempted: The preceding construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, common raywise Foelner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. These yield path-independent operators and explicit translation-boundary ratios. The collar induction nevertheless becomes circular if its trace is defined from the already-glued rule, while constant lower-skeleton extension can activate an unsafe candidate. By directive, no further generic averaging reroll is asserted as a proof.
obligation.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\),
\(\text{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\) proves that,
for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path, together with the bounds
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq2\min\{1,a/L\}
\]
and
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
The smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted path results separately give
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
\]
for each fixed finite library.  These conclusions control a single smoothed
ancestor, individual chart averages, path-independent common-ray operators,
and the error of an already specified finite gluing family.  They do not prove
canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate,
compatibility throughout simultaneous collar supports, translated-uniform
tails, or a computable growing-refinement schedule.  Hence the simultaneous
effective-compatible-density conclusion remains open.
